artifacts.synopsis: A ruling elder appealed convictions for distributing an SJC decision contrary to Session's will and for allegedly false, divisive statements in an email opposing a pastoral-election proposal. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed Session and Presbytery in whole, rendered not guilty, removed the indefinite suspension, and restored him to office. Session could not bind conscience without scriptural authority, and no express prohibition or proof of falsity existed. Many other specifications were rejected; a concurrence cautioned that such emails are rarely wise.

artifacts.title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination 'vetting' removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1's sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session's sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.

artifacts.synopsis: Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot.
